races.title: State House, District 11
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Allison A. Dahle
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina House District 11 (Raleigh) since January 2019. Raleigh native. Former theatre stage manager, then disability-employment specialist at the Young Adult Institute, The ARC of NC and Columbus Industries. Worked at a Raleigh law firm after 2003.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina listed as endorsing Dahle in 2026 (Ballotpedia).
Center for Freethought Equality listed as endorsing Dahle in 2026 (Ballotpedia).
Several voter-guide groups on Ballotpedia's Sway platform recommended her in 2026: Better Future NC, Brit in Raleigh's Voting Guide, Unburdening The Ballot, and Waves of Democracy.

cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or stated positions by Dahle on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. The Ballotpedia page lists her bills only as an empty table, so we could not confirm any she sponsored. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. No controversies, foreign ties, or public statements on data centers or development turned up in the pages reviewed. Her exact birth year is not given. Her campaign biography does not say what her role was at the Raleigh law firm.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign biography says she was born at Raleigh's old Rex Hospital, spent most of her childhood in Raleigh, graduated from Broughton High School, and moved back to Raleigh full-time in 2003.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since January 2019 (seven years). Earlier worked as a theatre stage manager, then as a community rehabilitation specialist and supported-employment program lead for people with disabilities (Young Adult Institute, The ARC of NC, Columbus Industries), and later at a local law firm.
qual.why: Several terms of legislative service put her in the high band. Committee vice-chair posts add nothing. Her career work was program administration, and her role at the law firm is not stated, so she is placed at the low end of the range.

cands.name: Matthew Kordon
cands.bio: Libertarian candidate for NC House District 11 in 2024 and 2026. Computer programmer and founder of a game development business (2018). Former Dell Technologies employee. Part-time paralegal since May 2026. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Fair Map Fight Club (Sway voting group by Tara Arbitter) listed him as a 2026 endorsement or voter guide recommendation.
In 2024 he reported endorsements from the Wild Caucus within the Libertarian Party and US Term Limits. This is self-reported, though Ballotpedia notes he signed the U.S. Term Limits Pledge.

cands.gaps: We could not find the year he moved to North Carolina or the exact date he moved to Cary. He has held no elected office, so there is no record of official actions. We found no stated positions on data centers, abortion, policing, immigration or H-1B, foreign or big-donor money, or limits on investor or foreign land buyers. His statements on housing and growth were too general to count either way. He says he wrote an "Environmental Stewardship" plank adopted at the 2026 Libertarian Party of NC convention, but we could not read its text. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his 2026 positions come only from his campaign site and his 2024 survey answers.

local.label: Roots 90: He was born in Maryland but says he grew up in Raleigh, graduated from Wakefield High in 2015, earned a UNC Wilmington degree, and now lives in Cary.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Founded a game development business in 2018 and still leads it. Worked as a software engineer at Dell Technologies through 2024. Took a part-time paralegal job in May 2026. Has no elected or legislative experience.
qual.why: Business ownership and work as a programmer and paralegal fit the middle band. He has no legislative, local-office or budget record.
qual.label: Business ownership and work as a programmer and paralegal fit the middle band. He has no legislative, local-office or budget record.

second-amendment.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he would "return your full right to own firearms and ammunition to be carried in public."

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he supports public schools, charters, religious schools, microschools and homeschooling, and that teacher wages would rise to keep pace with nearby states.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he wants to reduce overall taxes and spending. His campaign site criticizes the Town of Cary for expenditures that increase local property taxes.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised
